story_type: first American spacewalk: astronaut floats outside on a tether over the Earth, historic color film
hook: Outside the spacecraft, with only a cord holding him on.
narration: Ed White floated outside his spacecraft, with nothing but a cord holding him on.
June 1965. Gemini 4 carried Air Force test pilots James McDivitt and Ed White, both new to space.
Their Titan rocket sent them off on a four day flight, sixty two orbits around the Earth.
Four hours and twenty nine minutes in, White opened the hatch and made American history.
He steered himself with a small handheld gun that pushed him around with jets of gas.
outcome: White climbed back inside, and the two space pilots received a boisterous welcome aboard a Navy carrier.
title: First American to step into space
question_comment: Would you have stepped out of that hatch?

facts.claim: McDivitt and White, Air Force test pilots, new to space
facts.source_quote: Astronauts James McDibbit and Ed White were both new to space but not new to flight.
Both were crack Air Force test pilots.
The flight date, June 3, was a month earlier than originally planned.
GT4 was committed to 62 revolutions, four full days.
Four hours and twenty-nine minutes into the mission, Ed White made American history.
The two space pilots received a boisterous welcome aboard the Navy's USS1.

description:
Ed White floats outside Gemini 4 on a tether in June 1965, the first American spacewalk, during a four-day flight with James McDivitt.
